what_its_for: Glasdegib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukemia (AML). It is used together with a low-dose chemotherapy called cytarabine for adults who are newly diagnosed with AML and who cannot tolerate stronger chemotherapy treatments. It works by blocking a signal in cancer cells that helps them grow and survive.
how_to_take: Take glasdegib by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose or temporarily stop your treatment if you have side effects. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed and do not change it without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and your next scheduled dose is more than 12 hours away, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If your next dose is in less than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store glasdegib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Do not take glasdegib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm or cause death to an unborn baby. Both male and female patients must use effective birth control during treatment and for a period of time after stopping — talk to your doctor about the right type of contraception for you. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the amount of this medicine in your body and raise your risk of side effects. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines, or heart medicines, because many drugs can interact with glasdegib.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: irregular or fast heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting (which could be signs of a heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation); muscle cramps, spasms, or weakness; numbness or tingling; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; signs of low blood counts such as fever, chills, unusual bruising or bleeding, or feeling very tired; or if you are pregnant or think you might be pregnant. Also tell your doctor about any new or worsening symptoms, especially hair loss, changes in taste, or swelling.
when_it_works: Glasdegib begins working in your body right away, but it may take several weeks or months before you or your doctor can see or measure its full effect on your leukemia. Your doctor will do regular blood tests and check-ups to monitor how well the treatment is working. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own even if you do not feel different — always talk to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Glasdegib must NOT be used during pregnancy because it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Females who can become pregnant must have a pregnancy test before starting treatment and must use highly effective birth control during treatment and for at least 30 days after the last dose. Males with female partners who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 30 days after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking glasdegib and for at least 30 days after the last dose. Older adults (age 75 and older): Glasdegib has been used in older adults, but side effects may be more common. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
